evidence.fact: On January 13, 2026, the U.S. Department of Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) released a final rule revising the license review posture for NVIDIA H200- and AMD MI325X-equivalent chips and lesser-performance variants exported to PRC companies from a 'presumption of denial' to 'case-by-case review'.
evidence.source: Mayer Brown / U.S. Bureau of Industry and Security

evidence.fact: On January 21, 2026, the U.S. House Foreign Affairs Committee advanced the AI OVERWATCH Act (42–2), which proposes a two-year statutory restriction prohibiting the sale of advanced chips like Nvidia's Blackwell architecture to foreign entities of concern including China, Iran, North Korea, Russia, and Venezuela.
evidence.source: ML Strategies / House Foreign Affairs Committee

evidence.fact: On March 20, 2026, the White House released the National Policy Framework for Artificial Intelligence, outlining legislative recommendations and a federal strategy intended to secure U.S. dominance and check state-level regulatory fragmentation.
On April 2, 2026, the MATCH Act was introduced in the U.S. Congress with bipartisan cosponsors to further regulate semiconductor manufacturing equipment flowing to Chinese fabrication facilities.
Data published in April 2026 indicates that the United States controls approximately 75% of global AI compute capacity, while China holds 15%.

On June 2, 2026, President Trump signed Executive Order 14409, titled 'Promoting Advanced Artificial Intelligence Innovation and Security,' establishing new cybersecurity and national security directives focused on public-private defenses and secure frontier model benchmarks.
evidence.source: The White House / McDermott Will & Schulte

evidence.fact: On July 14, 2026, the Trump administration launched the 'GOLD EAGLE' initiative—a joint public-private clearinghouse implemented by the Treasury, Homeland Security, and Defense departments pursuant to EO 14409—to apply frontier AI models to vulnerability data and software threat remediation.

On July 22, 2026, the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy (OSTP) announced more than $5 billion in federal commitments expanding the Genesis Mission to accelerate AI-driven scientific discovery.
evidence.source: Mintz / Office of Science and Technology Policy
